title: Staff Noncommissioned Officer Academy Faculty Advisor (MGySgt to SSgt) EMOS, CG TECOM
raw_text:
16. MOS 0961, Staff Noncommissioned Officer Academy Faculty Advisor (MGySgt
to SSgt) EMOS, CG TECOM

    a. Summary. Marines assigned to a teaching billet or faculty position,
who facilitate learning as their primary duty in a designated course approved
by the appropriate general/flag officer in their chain of command, may be
granted an EMOS if they meet the prerequisites and requirements outlined
below. Augmented personnel support used to supplement training (e.g., role
players or demonstrator cadre) do not meet the criteria to be instructors.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must be in a full duty status.

            (2) Must have completed required PME for current grade.

        (3) Must meet Marine Corps height, weight, and body composition
standards.

        (4) Must be a staff sergeant or above. This prerequisite is
waiverable by the College of Enlisted Military Education.



                                          3-101                        Enclosure (1)
 3115                                                           NAVMC 1200.1L



       c.   Requirements

        (1) Approved award of the EMOS by the College of Enlisted Military
Education director.

        (2) Complete the Faculty Advisors Course (M02LAZ5) conducted at
Marine Corps Base Quantico, VA.

        (3) Achieve certification as a senior faculty advisor in the College
of Enlisted Military Educations Master Faculty Advisor Program.

        (4) Serve in a specified EDCOM faculty advisor designated billet
identification code (BIC) billet for a period of not less than 6 months.

        (5) Must meet the prerequisites prescribed in MCO 1553.2D Marine
Corps Formal School Management Policy Guidance.

        (6) Demonstrated level of proficiency and successful completion of
the duties associated with this EMOS while serving in an instructor billet.

        (7) CG EDCOM will be the approving authority for all waivers where
Marines are not currently assigned to fill a designated instructor billet
BIC, time serving in the billet, and any other request which does not meet
the requirements listed above.

       d.   Duties

        (1) Collaborate with formal school staff responsible for learning
design to ensure seamless transition into course implementation.

        (2) Employ MarineNet eLearning ecosystem to enable learner self-study
with accountability.

        (3) Prepare for and facilitate learning during specific course
lessons to achieve learning objectives and associated learning outcomes that
meet service defined common or occupational learning requirements.

        (4) Cultivate and sustain open and challenging learning environments
within lessons to prompt learners to engage and collaborate.

        (5) Guide lesson activities and debriefs, exploiting learning
opportunities as they emerge, per approved lesson files, course learning
outcomes, and local faculty qualification requirements.

        (6) Lead active learner-centered methods, using adult learning
methodologies including, gallery walks, discussions, decision-forcing cases,
decision games, practical applications, culminating events and wargaming
opportunities among others.

        (7) Provide formative and summative assessment to students per
approved rubrics to assess learning and provide learners with both
qualitative and quantitative feedback while maintaining the integrity of each
action.

        (8) Mentor and coach students regarding their academic progress,
learning, and professional and personal development.




                                    3-102                        Enclosure (1)
 3115                                                               NAVMC 1200.1L



        (9) Continue personal and professional development through feedback
collection, learning trends research, reflection, critical self-assessment,
goal setting, developmental course and activity completion, and confirmed
performance improvement.

        (10) Process lesson evaluation data and form recommendations to
support course review boards.

        (11) Professionally contribute to review boards and working groups
related to resource optimization in meeting defined service-learning
requirements.

        (12) Create customized lesson plans, decision-forcing case studies,
and faculty development sessions to develop professional and ethical
competence among peers and students.

        (13) Provide constructive criticism to peers and subordinates on the
effectiveness of their lessons.

            (14) Model and foster the Marine Corps culture of learning.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Teachers and Instructors, all other 25-3099.

       f.   Related Military Skill

            (1) Drill Instructor, 0911.

            (2) Marine Combat Instructor, 0913.

            (3) Formal School Instructor, 0951.

            (4) MAGTF Enlisted Instructor, 0981.
common_text: Occupational Field 09, Training, comprises MOSs used to identify Marines who possess skill sets to conduct vital training, particularly to entry-level Marines, as required by various high visibility Marine Corps programs. First exposure to Marine Corps training is provided by the Drill Instructor. Next contact is with the marksmanship coaches and instructors overseen by a Range Officer, Swim Instructors, Martial Arts Instructors, and then Marine Combat Instructors. In the operating forces, training continues with the addition of Small Weapons Instructors and Martial Arts Instructor-Trainers. These MOSs are sponsored by the Training and Education Command.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
